No tool was added or removed — the server still declares 110 — and the
server code is unchanged. What is new is beside the bundle: from this release
on, every release publishes the inventory of the dependencies it ships. The
bundle itself is rebuilt with dotenv 18.

## SBOM

`garmin-mcp-ts.sbom.cdx.json`, attached below, is a Software Bill of
Materials in [CycloneDX](https://cyclonedx.org/) 1.6 format. It lists the 139
production and optional dependencies that go into the `.mcpb`, each with its
declared licence, Package URL and tarball hash. It is generated from
`package-lock.json` by `@cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm` in reproducible mode, so it
describes exactly the bundle of this release and only changes when a
dependency does.

You can scan it for known vulnerabilities without installing anything:

```
grype sbom:garmin-mcp-ts.sbom.cdx.json
trivy sbom garmin-mcp-ts.sbom.cdx.json
```

The same file lives at the root of the repository as `sbom.cdx.json`, where
`npm run check:sbom` fails CI whenever it drifts from the lockfile. See the
[SBOM section of the README](https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts#-sbom-software-bill-of-materials)
for the details.

## Version updates

- **dotenv** 17.4.2 → 18.0.0 — a major release. `.env.vault` support and
  `node -r dotenv/config` preloading are removed; the `dotenv/config` import
  the login helper uses is still there, and the "injected env" message now
  goes to stderr instead of stdout, which is one risk fewer for a server that
  speaks MCP over stdio. The server keeps calling
  `config({ processEnv, quiet })` as before and its behaviour is unchanged.
- **@types/node** 26.4.1 → 26.6.1 — development only, not shipped in the
  bundle.

`npm audit` on this release reports no vulnerabilities.

## Install

Download `garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb` and open it with Claude Desktop, or drag it onto
Settings → Extensions. Verify the download first:

```
sha256sum -c garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb.sha256
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts/compare/v4.5.10...v4.6.0
